I've confirmed two declarers: the s3presign Runner is actually invoked in production code and internally in its ticker loop, while the memopayload Runner is never invoked anywhere and its constructor is also unused. I also checked the s3presign test file to see if it calls RunOnce, but it doesn't appear to.

Actually, the RebuildMemoPayload package-level function is used in production, though the RunOnce method itself isn't -- so I should double-check the runner_test.go for s3presign to confirm what counts as a test caller.

h08.

Exactly two types declare `RunOnce`, both named `Runner` but in different packages, and only one of them is ever called.

- `*s3presign.Runner` (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:43`) — yes, invoked — `server/server.go:163`, inside `startBackgroundRunners`, which runs one synchronous sweep at startup. It's also invoked internally by its own ticker loop `Runner.Run` at `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:36`, so the 12-hourly repeats go through the same method.
- `*memopayload.Runner` (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:27`) — no, never invoked — no caller anywhere in the repository.

How I verified: grepping all 343 non-`web` Go files for `RunOnce` yields only five hits total — the two declarations, the two `s3presign` call sites above, and the doc comment at `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:26`. No test calls either method; `server/runner/s3presign/runner_test.go` contains no reference to `RunOnce`, `Run`, or `CheckAndPresign`.

The `memopayload` runner is fully dead as a runner: its constructor `memopayload.NewRunner` (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:19`) has no callers either. The package is still live in production, but only via its package-level function `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload`, called from `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108` (memo creation) and `:447` (memo update) — the same function `RunOnce` would loop over every memo to apply as a backfill.
